info.name: Learn-E API
info.description: All product endpoints plus health, grouped by build phase. Every endpoint is implemented (Phases A to H); none returns 501. Contracts and current status are in docs/POSTMAN.md. Requests send Authorization: Bearer {{sessionToken}}; run Auth > Log in first to fill it, and Log out runs last. Get challenge uses expectedChallengeView for professor/learner response checks. Never store a database URI, GitHub token, Gemini API key, password or session token in this collection.

request.description: B-15/B-16: owning professor of the classroom only. Generates one field from the editor's current values without creating or saving a challenge. field is prompt, codeSnippet, explanation or appliedCasePrompt. title, language and objective are always required; codeSnippet also needs prompt, and explanation and appliedCasePrompt also need prompt and codeSnippet. Only those preceding fields reach Gemini. 200 { data: { field, content } }. A bad classroom id, unsupported field or missing prerequisite is 400 CONTENT_DRAFT_INVALID. Missing configuration is 503 CONTENT_DRAFTS_UNAVAILABLE, upstream 429 is 503 CONTENT_DRAFTS_RATE_LIMITED, other upstream/network/timeout/output failures are 502 CONTENT_DRAFTS_FAILED. Each successful send spends real Gemini free-tier quota.

request.description: Owning professor only (H-11). Removes a draft for good. 204 with no body; a published challenge answers 409 CHALLENGE_PUBLISHED, so running this after Publish challenge leaves the challenge in place.

One block per request (C-1). One Attempt per student and challenge; every submission is appended to answers as { questionId, value, correct, submittedAt } (C-2). 201 when this creates the Attempt, 200 when it adds to it (C-10). Set questionId to a real block id from Get challenge. The reply's unlockedHints lists the progressive hints unlocked so far, one per wrong answer (H-7).
Body field matches the stored field (C-11). The owner may replace a pending diagnosis until it is reviewed (C-7); approved work is final and returns 409 (C-6).
decision is approve or return (C-12); feedback is required on return (C-13). Approval is what unlocks mentoring for that challenge.

Question help (H-14): contextType "challenge", contextId a published challenge in a classroom you belong to, questionId one block id from Get challenge, and a hintType. No text fields. Only a classmate whose applied diagnosis for that challenge was approved can claim it. classroomId is derived from the challenge on the server. If your last answer to that question was wrong, the server saves it in plain words as askerAnswer (H-22).

General class help (H-14): contextType "classroom", contextId your classroom, and codeSnippet, expectedBehaviour and actualBehaviour (all required after trim) plus a hintType. Any other member of the classroom can claim it.

{
  "contextType": "classroom",
  "contextId": "{{classroomId}}",
  "codeSnippet": "for (let i = 0; i <= n; i++) total += i",
  "expectedBehaviour": "Adds 0 to n - 1",
  "actualBehaviour": "Also adds n",
  "hintType": "Guiding question"
}

request.description: No official answer may appear in this response. A question help request carries challengeCode, the challenge's code snippet (H-22). askerAnswer, the asker's last wrong answer, is sent only to the asker, the claiming mentor, the owning professor and members who could claim the request.
The winning mentor repeating the claim gets 200; anyone else gets 409 (D-7).
At most 1000 characters after trim (D-9). The assigned mentor may overwrite the hint until the request is resolved (D-8).
A repeat helpful returns 200 and awards nothing (D-10). Unresolved clears claimedBy, mentorResponse and helpful and increments reopenCount (D-3, G-8).

item.name: Mini-projects and groups (Phase E, F, G)

request.description: Saves a new draft (H-8). Only the title is required; every other field is checked for type and may be left blank until publishing. Blank criteria are dropped, and a blank starterRepoUrl or qualifyingChallengeId means none. Students can't see a draft. qualifyingChallengeId must be a published challenge in this classroom (E-2). maxGroupSize has no upper limit (E-3) and defaults to 2. The starter repository is shown as a link and never fetched (F-2). Copy the returned id into miniProjectId, then Publish mini-project.

body.raw:
{
  "title": "Event registration repair",
  "brief": "Diagnose and repair the registration flow.",
  "starterRepoUrl": "https://github.com/example/starter",
  "maxGroupSize": 4,
  "qualifyingChallengeId": "{{challengeId}}",
  "stageInstructions": {
    "Diagnose": "Symptoms and causes",
    "Repair": "Fixes mapped to criteria",
    "Extend": "One small feature",
    "Verify": "Tests or repeatable checks",
    "Reflect": "Why the repair works"
  },
  "acceptanceCriteria": [
    "Works on a phone",
    "Rejects invalid sign-ups"
  ],
  "rubric": "Evidence quality"
}

request.description: Owning professor only (H-8). Saves changes to a draft; fields left out keep their saved values, and the same draft rules as Create apply. A published brief answers 409 MINIPROJECT_PUBLISHED, because published briefs can't be edited. status, createdBy and classroomId in the body are ignored.

Owning professor only (H-8). Checks the saved draft: title, brief, rubric, all five stage instructions and at least one acceptance criterion must be filled in, and a qualifying challenge must still be published in this classroom. Problems come back together as 400 VALIDATION_FAILED and the brief stays a draft. Success is 200 with status published; publishing again answers the same brief.
The owning professor sees every group's full workspace (E-6). Note the group's updatedAt for Replace tasks.

Owning professor only, while the brief is a draft (H-10). Choose a PDF or zip as the binary body and put its URI-encoded name in X-File-Name. Files can be up to 4 MB (larger answers 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE; H-23) and a brief holds at most 5. The server checks the file's first bytes, so a renamed program answers 400 VALIDATION_FAILED. A published brief answers 409 MINIPROJECT_PUBLISHED. 201 with { id, name, size, contentType, uploadedAt }; copy the id into materialId.

Anyone who can open the brief (H-10): the owning professor, or a member student once it is published (a student gets 404 for a draft's file). Answers the file as an attachment with its original name. Use Send and Download in Postman to save it.
Owning professor only, while the brief is a draft (H-10). Removes the file from the brief and from storage. 204 with no body; a published brief answers 409 MINIPROJECT_PUBLISHED.
Joining a group you are already in returns 200; another group in the same project or a full group is 409 (E-7).
Whole-array replacement guarded by updatedAt (E-8): send the group's updatedAt from Get mini-project; a stale value gets 409 and the page reloads.
Merge by stage key: only the stages present in the body change (E-5).

Implemented F4 (F-1, F-5): group members only. Body { repositoryUrl } must be a public https://github.com/owner/repo link; a trailing slash, .git and surrounding spaces are accepted and stored as https://github.com/owner/repo. A changed link clears the cached GitHub snapshot; sending the link already attached changes nothing. Nothing is fetched from GitHub here (that is Refresh GitHub data). 200 { data: { id, repositoryUrl, updatedAt } }. Missing or blank link is 400 VALIDATION_FAILED (field repositoryUrl); any other link is 400 INVALID_GITHUB_REPOSITORY_URL; no selected user 401, bad id 400, outsider 403, missing group 404 GROUP_NOT_FOUND.

request.description: Implemented F5 (F-3, F-6): group members and the owning professor. Empty body. Fetches the attached repository, its five latest commits and its top 10 contributors (F-7) from api.github.com, then saves them as the group's snapshot with a new lastRefreshedAt. 200 { data: { repositoryUrl, repository, commits, contributors, lastRefreshedAt } }. No link attached is 409 REPOSITORY_NOT_ATTACHED (GitHub is not called); a link changed during the refresh is 409 REPOSITORY_CHANGED. A GitHub failure returns only its named error and leaves the old snapshot untouched: 404 GITHUB_REPOSITORY_NOT_FOUND, 400 GITHUB_REPOSITORY_PRIVATE, 429 GITHUB_RATE_LIMITED, 502 GITHUB_UNAVAILABLE. Each send spends three requests of real GitHub quota (60 an hour without a server token).

request.description: Implemented G1 (G-1, G-2, G-3): group members only. Body { reflection }. Needs non-empty Diagnose, Repair and Verify evidence in the saved group plus a reflection of 1 to 5000 characters after trimming; every gap is listed at once in a 400 VALIDATION_FAILED whose details name stageEvidence.Diagnose, stageEvidence.Repair, stageEvidence.Verify or reflection. Draft or returned work moves to submitted; any earlier professorFeedback is kept. 200 { data: { id, submissionStatus, reflection, professorFeedback, updatedAt } }. Work already submitted or approved (approved is final) is 409 INVALID_SUBMISSION_STATUS, as is a submit that loses a race with another member.

request.description: Implemented G2 (G-4, G-5): the professor who owns the classroom only; group members get 403. Body { decision, feedback } with decision "approve" or "return"; feedback is required on a return (400 VALIDATION_FAILED otherwise). Only submitted work can be reviewed: anything else, or a review that loses a race, is 409 INVALID_REVIEW_STATUS. Sets only submissionStatus (approved or returned) and professorFeedback; stage evidence and reflection stay. 200 { data: { id, submissionStatus, professorFeedback, updatedAt } }.

request.description: Owning professor only (H-11). Removes a draft and its uploaded files for good. 204 with no body; a published brief answers 409 MINIPROJECT_PUBLISHED, so running this after Publish mini-project leaves the brief in place.

Owning professor or member student (H-15). The professor gets { viewer: "professor", game } with the full editable game, or game null before the first save. A student gets { viewer: "student", game, play, defeated }: game is null unless one is published, and otherwise holds only the title, monster, hearts and question count. play is their run in progress or null, and its current question never says which answer is right. Anyone else is 403.

exec: pm.test("A student's copy hides the questions and right answers", function () {

request.description: Owning professor only (H-15). The editor's autosave target: the first save creates the draft (201), later saves update it (200). Send only the fields you change. A draft only has to be well formed: bossId is one of null-slime, infinite-wyrm, off-by-one-golem, memory-kraken, race-ghost or syntax-spider, hearts is 1 to 10, at most 50 questions, and each question and answer needs its own id (letters, digits, - or _). Bad input is 400 VALIDATION_FAILED with a field per problem. A published game is 409 GAME_PUBLISHED until it is unpublished.

Owning professor only (H-15). Needs the server's GEMINI_API_KEY and GEMINI_MODEL, the same settings as Generate challenge content. Give a topic or some code, and count 1 to 10 (default 5). Returns { questions } and saves nothing: the editor adds them as drafts the professor approves. 400 GAME_DRAFT_INVALID for a bad request, 503 GAME_DRAFTS_UNAVAILABLE without a key, 503 GAME_DRAFTS_RATE_LIMITED, 502 GAME_DRAFTS_FAILED. Each send spends real quota.

Owning professor only (H-15). Checks the saved game, not the request: a title, a monster, at least three questions, and for each one its text, at least two different answers, a right answer, a Why? explanation and no unapproved generated draft. Problems come back together as 400 VALIDATION_FAILED. Success is 200 with status published, and each publication starts fresh results. Publishing again changes nothing. No game yet is 404 GAME_NOT_FOUND.

Owning professor only (H-15, H-20). Results for the current publication: how many played and won, per-question first-try accuracy and the most common wrong answer, and a students list with each member's name, attempts and best result (won, lost, playing or not-played). It never shows which answers a student picked. A student is 403.

Member student only (H-15). Starts a run (201) or returns the one already in progress (200) as { play }. Its test saves play.id into gamePlayId and the current question's id into gameQuestionId; set gameOptionId to one of that question's answer ids before Answer game play. No published game is 404 GAME_NOT_FOUND; the professor or a non-member is 403.

exec: pm.test("Returns a run with an id", () => pm.expect(play.id).to.be.a("string"));

request.description: The student who owns the run (H-15, H-20). Answers the current question only. answerCount (optional) is how many answers the browser has seen, so a stale tab can't spend a heart. Replies { correct, explanation, play }. explanation is empty after a wrong answer, since that question comes back (H-20); What to review lists it at the end. A wrong question or a changed game is 409 PLAY_CHANGED, an option that isn't offered is 400 VALIDATION_FAILED, someone else's run is 403.

exec: pm.test("A wrong answer gives no explanation away", function () {

request.description: Owning professor only (H-15). Returns the game to a draft so it can be edited, and ends every run in progress. Safe to repeat. No game yet is 404 GAME_NOT_FOUND.
Sends a header that is not "Bearer <token>". Expect 401 INVALID_SESSION, with or without a database.
Expect 404 NOT_FOUND.

The claiming mentor only (H-12, UX audit A3). No body. Returns a claimed request to open with claimedBy cleared; reopenCount is unchanged. 200 { id, status: "open", mentorId: null }. Once a hint is sent it is 409 INVALID_STATE, so after Respond to help request this run answers 409.

The requester only (H-12, UX audit A2). Deletes the request while it is still open: 200 { id, withdrawn: true }. A claimed, responded or resolved request is 409 INVALID_STATE, which is what this run gets after Resolve help request.

Group members only (H-12, UX audit A4). No body. Allowed while the group's work is draft or returned, otherwise 409 INVALID_STATE. The leaver's tasks stay without an owner, and the last member out deletes the group. 200 { id, left: true, groupDeleted }.

Students only (H-12, UX audit A4). No body. 409 IN_A_GROUP while the student is in a group of one of the classroom's mini-projects. Otherwise removes the membership and its points, withdraws the student's open help requests and returns their unanswered claims to the queue; attempts stay. 200 { classroomId, left: true }.

Owning professor only (H-12, UX audit A6). Deletes the classroom and everything in it: attempts, help requests, groups, uploaded files, mini-projects, challenges and memberships. 204 with no body. It runs last on purpose: it removes the records this run created, so nothing after it needs them.
G16. Ends this session only: 204 with no body. Runs last so the other requests keep the session. Without a session it is 401.
